signals.text: Homepage review box shows a one-star review near the top; typos 'Trading Standards Appoved' and 'we will be give you a clear of'

bestTime: Tue to Thu, 8 to 9am or 4:30 to 5:30pm

sections.label: Before you dial
sections.body:
Who: Gavin, director at LCL Landscaping and Groundcare, Motherwell.
Why them: good site, ranks #1 in Motherwell, but the homepage review box shows a one-star review near the top and there are a couple of typos.
Best time: Tue to Thu, 8 to 9am or 4:30 to 5:30pm.
Ltd company: tick CTPS (and TPS if it's a personal mobile) in the desk before you dial.
What you want: a 15-minute chat, on the phone or you pop in.
Stand up, slow down on your name, and stop talking after every question.

sections.label: If someone else answers
sections.body:
Hi, it's Dean Finlayson, is Gavin about?
_(if they ask what it's about)_ It's about how folk find LCL online. Is Gavin the right person for that, or is it someone else?
_(if Gavin is out)_ No bother. When's the best time to catch them? _(write their name in the note)_

sections.label: Opener
sections.body:
Hi Gavin, it's Dean Finlayson from Level One from Edinburgh. _(slow)_
The reason I'm calling is your homepage. Your site's one of the best I've seen for landscaping, but there's one thing on it you'll want to know about. Is now OK for 30 seconds?
_(stop and wait)_

sections.label: Why I'm calling
sections.body:
The review box on your homepage is showing a one-star review near the top. And there are two typos, Trading Standards Appoved is one. Easy fixes.
_(if they say go on)_ How much of your work comes from people looking you up first?

sections.label: Questions
sections.body:
Q: How are you getting reviews just now? Do you ask, or do they just come in?
Q: When did you last look at your own homepage the way a customer would?
Q: Where do most of your new jobs come from?
Listen for: reviews only coming in when they remember to ask, a bad review that's bothered them.

sections.label: If it's a problem for them
sections.body:
That's what I do. I'll send you the quick fixes for the homepage, and I set up a simple text that asks every happy customer for a Google review, so the good ones keep coming.
I'm local, I build it myself, and you deal with me, not a call centre.

sections.label: The ask
sections.body:
Easier to show you than explain. Fifteen minutes, on the phone or I'll pop in to you. Tuesday at 8, or Thursday after 5, which is better?
_(if they hesitate)_ No commitment. If it's not for you, no bother at all.

sections.label: If they push back
sections.body:
They: We already get good reviews.
You: You do, that's why I rang. It's just the one-star one sitting near the top of your homepage. Easy fix, and I'll show you how to keep the good ones coming.

They: I'm not interested.
You: Fair enough, most folk aren't till they know why I'm calling. Quick one before I go: is getting found online something you've got covered?

They: Send me an email.
You: Will do. So I don't send you something you'll bin, what matters more to you right now, more enquiries or less time on the phone?

They: How much is it?
You: Depends what you need. It's a one-off build and then a small monthly. I'd rather show you first than throw a number at you. Fifteen minutes, I could pop in?

They: Don't call me again.
You: No problem, I'll take you off. Sorry for the interruption, all the best. _(Log as Do not call)_

sections.body: Hi Gavin, it's Dean Finlayson from Level One from Edinburgh. I'm calling about a one-star review showing near the top of your homepage, easy fix. I'll drop you a text with what I mean. You can get me back on this number. Again, it's Dean from Level One. Cheers.
